items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: of playing in Europe with the Will Marion Cook band and as a soloist

ctx.x: That's the impression I got, but I never did hear it and I wasn't sure if that was right.

I think his early experience when he was, what, 19 years old, of playing in Europe with the Will Marion Cook band and as a soloist in front of what to him was a real concert orchestra made a tremendous impression on him. And all during his later life, that was sort of an ideal to be a great soloist before a huge orchestra, you know. Yeah. And Will Marion Cook was one of his idols in a sense.

items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: You know he went to France with Will Marion Cook’s Southern Syncopated Orchestra in 1919, not as a sideman in the band, he was a soloist.

ctx.x: Marvelous. Yeah. And pull the listener with you gradually.

Yeah. And he’d explain about jazz rhythm, he says jazz rhythm, you’ve got that steady beat going here, and then you introduce rhythms against the steady beat. That’s what jazz is. [scats] That’s what you’ve got to do, that steady beat and then those rhythms against it. He had a very strong idea about what he was doing. He considered himself an artist from the earliest days. You know he went to France with Will Marion Cook’s Southern Syncopated Orchestra in 1919, not as a sideman in the band, he was a soloist. He…
I think it’s an interesting statement you just said that he considered himself an artist from the beginning.
